title: Add @export_flags_grid and @export_flags_grid_named annotations

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

body: My take on https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/14004. This might require a follow-up PR for the [documentation](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/scripting/gdscript/gdscript_exports.html). Adds two new GDScript annotations that display bit flags using the compact layer grid UI instead of the vertical checklist: - @export_flags_grid(count) - unnamed flags shown in compact grid - @export_flags_grid_named("a", "b", "c") - named flags in compact grid This reuses EditorPropertyLayers and EditorPropertyLayersGrid with a new non-ProjectSettings code path. The grid now also stops drawing cells mid-block when the flag count is not a multiple of the group size. ## Reasoning My view here is that the user might or might not want to name their stats, and that there's no necessity for the user to control the layer grouping since it's purely visual (4 being the chosen sweet spot) There's lots of room for discussion on what should be the right approach UX-wise, any feedback is welcome. ### Testing Use: ``` @export_flags_grid_named("Health", "Attack", "Defense", "Speed", "Dexterity", "Intelligence", "Wisdom") var attributes @export_flags_grid(27) var unnamed_attributes @export_flags_2d_render var existing_functionality_2d_render @export_flags_2d_physics var existing_functionality_2d_physics @export_flags("a", "b") var existing_functionality_flags # uncomment below to see if error is valid # #@export_flags_grid(33) var test_error #@export_flags_grid_named("STR", "DEX", "CON", "INT", "WIS", "CHA", "HP", "MP", "ATK", "DEF", "SPD", "LCK", "CRT", "EVD", "ACC", "RES", "VIT", "AGI", "END", "FCS", "PER", "STL", "RGN", "DRN", "PRC", "BLK", "PSN", "BRN", "FRZ", "STN", "SIL", "CRS", "ThisOneExplodesBeyondLimit") var spell_elements = 0 ``` - Check visual results and experiment tweaking: - Hover mouse over named and un-named flags to see if the new and old functionality is correct. - Attempt renaming layers to see if new and old functionality is correct. New flags should not allow renaming, since they're either un-named or named but controlled via code.
